records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
search_queries: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
records.answer:
A J-1 master's student can do up to **18 months** of Academic Training (AT), or the length of their degree program if that is shorter. Students pursuing a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension. ([ISSS Academic Training page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/j1-employment))

Key conditions from that page:
- AT done while studying and AT done after the program ends are added together. Full-time and part-time AT count equally.
- The total employment/training period can't exceed the length of your academic program.
- AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date, and it must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.
- Submit the Academic Training form to ISSS at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends submitting at least three weeks ahead to allow for processing.

**Duration of status:** DHS published a final rule on July 17, 2026 that would eliminate duration of status. On September 14, 2026, a federal court postponed its effective date and barred DHS from implementing it ([court update](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status)). ISSS says it is monitoring the situation. The ISSS pages I found don't say how this would change AT limits.

For your own situation, including the STEM extension, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.
